sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, pushing Gemini 4-class speed and agentic coding down to free users, while a second thread shows European enterprises swapping OpenAI and Anthropic coding assistants for open-weight Chinese models.

sections.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for fast coding and agentic workflows
sections.content: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, positioned for everyday coding and agentic tasks rather than deep reasoning, alongside the existing Carbon and Argon models. It offers four thinking levels, a 1M-token context window, API pricing of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, and rollout across Gemini app, Google Search, AI Studio, Gemini API, Gemini for Business and Antigravity, with free users able to access it via automatic model selection. Reported scores include 51 on the Artificial Analysis intelligence index at default high thinking (54 at xhigh), and Google also introduced an Orchestrator feature in Antigravity that switches between models within a session.
sections.significance: Extends the Gemini 4 family's frontier capability to free and mainstream tiers and targets the high-volume coding and agent use cases where model choice is most contested.
sections.transition_hint: Google's push to widen access to a frontier family contrasts with the next item, where a European fintech moved in the opposite direction — away from closed US models.

sections.title: Revolut replaces OpenAI and Anthropic coding assistants with Zhipu's open GLM models
sections.content: At the Web Summit in Lisbon, co-founder Paddy Cosgrave said UK fintech Revolut has replaced the OpenAI and Anthropic coding assistants it previously used with Zhipu's open-source GLM series. Revolut's AI infrastructure lead David Abitbol said GLM is now the default coding model for roughly 2,000 engineers, with average coding time down about 60% and AI-related call costs down nearly 90% since rollout. The same reporting cites AFP noting Chinese open models are downloadable and modifiable, in contrast to closed US models, and that Orange, Renault and Siemens have publicly said they use DeepSeek and Qwen models as supplements.
sections.significance: A concrete enterprise displacement of two leading US vendors by an open-weight Chinese model, with cost and latency figures attached, signaling open models as a real procurement alternative in Europe.
sections.transition_hint: The open-model shift lands directly on Anthropic's enterprise franchise, which is the subject of the next item's IPO analysis.

sections.title: Anthropic IPO analysis details Claude roadmap, enterprise economics and risks
sections.content: A Gate Square analysis of Anthropic's public prospectus and product progress says Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, released November 9, 2026, are positioned as its strongest models, citing a 49.1% FrontierCode 2.0 score and 64.9% success on a simulated dual-arm robot test. It reports H1 2026 revenue of $16.286 billion, Q2 revenue of $11.555 billion up 1,368% year over year, a first quarterly operating profit of $974 million at about 8.4% margin, and a net loss of $80.748 billion driven mostly by $72.388 billion in non-cash fair-value changes. It also cites plans to list on Nasdaq under ticker ANT around mid-November 2026, with reported valuation discussions of $1.5–2 trillion against a $965 billion post-H轮 valuation, and flags slowing sequential growth (45% in Q3 vs 144% in Q2) and compute constraints.
sections.significance: Puts hard financial and product numbers around Anthropic's listing and its enterprise-first compute allocation, framing the competitive pressure from OpenAI and cheaper open-weight models.
sections.transition_hint: From Anthropic's enterprise economics, the next item turns to a developer-tooling release from DeepSeek.

sections.title: DeepSeek Harness preview adds per-session AgentTeam orchestration
sections.content: DeepSeek Harness v0.2.2-rc.2, a preview release dated November 11, adds a per-session AgentTeam panel showing team members and tasks, named sub-agents and layered collaboration. An accompanying analysis describes a Super-agent design with a Router dispatching tasks to Workers in separate sessions, threads grouped by pull request or chat topic, and an experimental subagent_oar tool that hands tasks to a local Codex or Claude Code install. Cross-session long-term memory is not built in; product team member Cui Tianyi is quoted saying it may be close, and the internal Super-agent prototype reportedly runs only in a small trusted environment.
sections.significance: Shows a Chinese lab shipping multi-agent orchestration into a developer harness while openly flagging durable cross-session memory as unsolved.
sections.transition_hint: DeepSeek's orchestration work is one piece of the broader agent-infrastructure buildout covered next.

sections.title: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro listed on NVIDIA NIM
sections.content: NVIDIA's NIM documentation on Build.NVIDIA.com lists Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro, dated November 4, 2026, as a multimodal model accepting text, image and video input with a 1,048,576-token context window and a mixture-of-experts architecture (2.8 trillion total, 104 billion active parameters). Reported benchmarks include 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 92.7% Voxel IoU with tools on a 1,000-file BenchCAD subset, with deployment optimized for vLLM with NVIDIA Dynamo on Blackwell GB300 under Linux. NVIDIA states the model is third-party built, and Moonshot reports reduced exploit capability after training-data filtering while noting residual dual-use cyber capability.
sections.significance: Puts a Chinese open multimodal model into NVIDIA's enterprise deployment channel with published agentic and CAD benchmarks.
sections.transition_hint: Kimi's distribution win is another data point in the same open-model momentum, but on the infrastructure side rather than enterprise procurement.

sections.title: Cross-Org Themes
content: Open-weight Chinese models gaining enterprise and infrastructure traction against closed US vendors
Agentic coding and multi-agent orchestration as the focal use case across releases

sections.title: Rumors and Unverified Claims
sections.content: Anthropic's reported Nasdaq listing under ticker ANT around mid-November 2026, with valuation discussions of $1.5–2 trillion, comes from a single third-party Gate Square analysis of prospectus and media reports and is not independently confirmed in the supplied material.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Watch whether Anthropic's listing and enterprise retention hold up against open-weight substitution, and whether Google's free-tier Hydrogen converts into developer share rather than just benchmark headlines.
